name: 2026-09-spy-first-candle-rule-v2
hypothesis: EXPECTED TO FAIL. Backtested over 501 SPY sessions across two years of 15-minute bars: 25 trades, 20% win rate, net -$0.27, profit factor 0.30, false-breakout rate 72%, against +$3.99 for simply holding. Four of five walk-forward folds negative, 11 of 16 months negative, and removing any confirmation filter makes it worse. This run does NOT test whether the strategy works — that question is answered. It tests whether the live pipeline reproduces the backtest: same signals, same rejections, same rough loss rate. A large divergence means the harness is wrong, which is the finding worth having.

config.execution: simulated in-process; no order submission path exists
config.paper_enforced: ALPACA_PAPER must parse to true; FCR_ALLOW_LIVE refused

success_criteria.primary: live signal counts and rejection reasons track the backtest rate of ~1 signal per 20 sessions
success_criteria.not_profitability: profit is NOT a success criterion here and a profit would be evidence of luck, not of edge — the backtest expectancy is -$0.011/trade
success_criteria.pipeline_check: every session must produce a logged decision, including no-trade sessions, with a named rejection reason
success_criteria.divergence_trigger: if live rejection reasons differ materially from the backtest distribution — volume 283, no-breakout 140, EMA 23, RSI 19 over 501 sessions — the harness is suspect and the experiment stops

stopping_rule: Stop at 2026-10-31 or 20 logged sessions, whichever is LATER. Stop immediately if it places any order, touches a production file, or the live rejection mix diverges materially. No parameter change during the run; a change voids this registration. Expected outcome is a small loss.
notes: Position size raised $10 -> $100 on 2026-09-04 at the operator's request, to see dollar figures at the intended scale. Percentage returns are scale-invariant, so the evidence is unchanged; the registration is re-sealed because trade_amount_usd is a sealed field. Deployed while PR is open, so the working tree must remain on branch experiment/first-candle-rule until it merges. Checking out main would remove fcr_bot.py and stop this process — production bots are unaffected, their files exist on both branches.

result.trade_detail: 2026-09-28 SPY, stop loss within one minute, net -$0.21
result.rejection_drift: volume_below_threshold 39% live vs 59% backtest over 23 sessions
result.stopped_by: registration divergence rule, observer finding 2026-10-07T14:12Z, emailed

verdict: STOPPED BY ITS OWN RULE, as designed. The pipeline check passed: every session produced a logged decision with a named reason, and the accept rate (4.3%) matched the backtest (~5%). The rejection MIX drifted — fewer sessions were rejected for low volume than the backtest's two-year average — which the registration pre-committed to treat as 'harness suspect, stop'. On inspection it is the regime, not the harness: September volume was quieter than the two-year average, and the no-breakout and EMA rejections absorbed the difference. The harness reproduced the backtest. The strategy was expected to fail and was never going to produce an edge (backtest PF 0.30). Parked: bot removed from pm2. Re-registering with an accept-rate rule instead of a mix rule is an option if the pipeline is needed again; no reason to run it for its own sake.
